items.en: A place to live or stay
items.ex: The college provides accommodation for students.
items.tip: Two c's and two m's: it accommodates both.

items.ex: Don't embarrass him in front of guests.
items.tip: Double r, double s: you go really red and smile shyly.

items.ex: Practice is necessary for success.
items.tip: One collar (c) and two sleeves (ss).

items.ex: Power cuts are a daily occurrence here.
items.tip: Double c, double r, then -ence.

items.ex: Keep the wet and dry waste separate.
items.tip: There is 'a rat' in separate.

items.ex: I will definitely attend the class.
items.tip: It comes from finite: de-finite-ly.

items.en: A group chosen for a task
items.ex: The committee approved the budget.
items.tip: Double m, double t, double e.

items.en: Inner sense of right and wrong
items.ex: His conscience did not let him lie.
items.tip: Con + science.

items.ex: Voting is a privilege and a duty.
items.tip: No 'd' in privilege; it ends like 'leg'.

items.en: A period of a thousand years
items.ex: The new millennium began in 2001.
items.tip: Double l and double n.

items.ex: I recommend this book for grammar.
items.tip: One c, two m's.

items.en: A regular repeated pattern of sound
items.ex: The song has a catchy rhythm.
items.tip: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move.

items.ex: Did you receive my parcel?
items.tip: I before E, except after C.

items.ex: The shop gives a one-year guarantee.
items.tip: Guard + antee: the guard gives a guarantee.

items.ex: The lift is closed for maintenance.
items.tip: Main-ten-ance: no 'tain' in the middle.

items.en: The way a word is spoken
items.ex: Her pronunciation is very clear.
items.tip: Pronounce loses its 'o': pro-nun-ciation.

items.ex: Please fill in the questionnaire.
items.tip: Double n, ends in -aire.

items.en: A person who starts a business
items.ex: The young entrepreneur opened three shops.
items.tip: Entre + pre + neur.

items.ex: The mischievous child hid the keys.
items.tip: Mischief + ous: no extra 'i' before -ous.

items.ex: She acts as liaison between the two teams.
items.tip: Two i's around the a: li-a-i-son.

items.ex: The lieutenant led the parade.
items.tip: Lie + u + tenant.

items.ex: Wear this dress for a special occasion.
items.tip: Double c, single s.

items.ex: The bill was passed in parliament.
items.tip: There is 'I am' in parliament.

items.ex: Persistent effort brings results.
items.tip: Ends in -ent, like 'consistent'.

items.ex: The new rules supersede the old ones.
items.tip: The only English word ending in -sede.

items.ex: The company cannot withhold your salary.
items.tip: With + hold: keep both h's.

items.ex: It is a crime to harass someone online.
items.tip: One r, two s's.

items.ex: He is an acquaintance, not a close friend.
items.tip: Ac-quaint-ance: keep the c before q.

items.ex: Too much bureaucracy slows decisions.
items.tip: Bureau + cracy.

items.en: Make something seem bigger than it is
items.ex: Don't exaggerate the problem.
items.tip: Double g, single x.

items.en: ownership of property or an item
items.ex: the stolen bicycle was found in his possession.
items.tip: remember it has double s twice: po-ss-e-ss-ion.

items.ex: a good flask keeps liquids hot by creating a vacuum inside.
items.tip: one v at the start, followed by two u letters.

items.ex: we will submit our project files tomorrow morning.
items.tip: to-morrow starts with to, then add morrow.

items.ex: the sudden assassination of the leader shocked the nation.
items.tip: ass-ass-in-ation: think of an ass twice in a nation.

items.ex: securing a government job is a big achievement for the family.
items.tip: i before e except after c rule applies: achieve.

items.ex: unprovoked aggression on the playground led to a match ban.
items.tip: double g and double s: ag-gress-ion.

items.ex: his lack of interest was apparent from his yawning.
items.tip: starts with ap, followed by parent.

items.ex: monsoon showers marked the beginning of the sowing season.
items.tip: double n before ing: begin-n-ing.

items.ex: small tea stalls do brisk business near railway stations.
items.tip: busy becomes business by adding ness.

items.ex: check the wall calendar to see festival dates.
items.tip: ends with ar like car, not er.

items.ex: She started her banking career after graduation.
items.tip: Care for your career with single r and double e at the end.

items.ex: The old cemetery is located near the mango orchard.
items.tip: Remember all 'e' vowels: c-e-m-e-t-e-r-y.

items.ex: The weather during monsoon is quite changeable.
items.tip: Keep the 'e' in change before adding 'able'.

items.ex: The brave colonel received a gallantry award.
items.tip: Pronounced like kernel, but spelled with two l's and no r in the middle.

items.en: a dedication to a cause or activity
items.ex: His commitment to social work is truly inspiring.
items.tip: Double m, double t: c-o-m-m-i-t-m-e-n-t.

items.en: wishing to do one's work well
items.ex: A conscientious employee never ignores small details.
items.tip: Contains 'science' in the middle: con-science-tious.

items.ex: The family reached a consensus regarding the vacation spot.
items.tip: Both parts start with 'con' and end with 'sus'.

items.ex: Choosing between higher studies and a job created a dilemma.
items.tip: Double 'l' and double 'm'? No, double 'm' only: d-i-l-e-m-m-a.

items.ex: Daily practice requires immense physical discipline.
items.tip: Dis-ci-pline: remember the middle 'ci'.

items.ex: The morning fog began to dissipate as the sun rose.
items.tip: Double 's' near the start, single 'p' in the middle.
